privacy: Files stay on your device. Nothing is uploaded.
inputHint: Drop subtitle files here or paste text below.
encodingHint: If text looks garbled, choose its original encoding and convert again.
fpsHint: Used for frame-based timestamps. Embedded frame rates take priority.
offsetHint: Positive values delay subtitles; negative values show them earlier.
emptyOutput: Convert a file or pasted text to preview the result.
previewLimit: Showing the first 100 cues. Downloads include all cues.
formatsHint: Convert between 19 text subtitle formats, or export a plain-text transcript. TTML input also accepts iTT files. SUB means MicroDVD or SubViewer; STL means text-based Spruce STL.
fidelity: Conversion keeps text, timing and supported basic formatting. Advanced styles and positioning may change. Files download as UTF-8.
bitmapHint: Image subtitles (PGS/SUP, VobSub/IDX) need OCR; binary EBU STL needs a subtitle editor.
transcriptNote: TXT exports readable text without timestamps.
estimatedNote: LRC and QuickTime text can omit end times. Missing ends use the next cue or 2 seconds for the final cue; LRC cannot retain gaps or overlapping end times.
shiftedNote: Cues shifted entirely before zero were removed; partially negative cues start at zero.
precisionNote: This format rounds times to centiseconds, tenths of a second or video frames.
empty: Add subtitle text or choose files first.
unsupported: The format could not be detected. Choose the input format or use one of the supported text subtitle formats.
invalid: Some subtitle content could not be read. Check the selected format and timestamps.
timing: Each cue needs a valid start and a later end time.
invalidOptions: Enter a frame rate from 1 to 120 and a numeric time offset.
readError: This file could not be read. Try selecting it again.
encodingError: This file could not be decoded with that encoding. Choose its original encoding in the settings.
noCues: No subtitle cues remain. Check the content and time offset.
jsonHint: JSON uses an array of {start, end, text} objects with times in milliseconds. CSV/TSV use start,end,text headers and millisecond or clock timestamps. Whisper segments with second-based times are also accepted.
